Hi Mina / Ben —

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. We're starting to assemble our side of the handoff artifacts and want to confirm the exact checklist items Redwood requires before the tenant activation window (target: Nov 9). High level asks from our infra team:

- Confirm service account formats and least-privilege IAM roles we should create on our GCP project.
- Public egress IPs / NAT ranges Redwood should allow for control-plane callbacks.
- KMS key metadata format (identifier + rotation policy) for secrets sync.
- Connectivity test targets (FQDNs + port list) and one-time troubleshooting ssh/jump host.

I've attached our initial access matrix (gravitas-access-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a preliminary network diagram. Can one of you confirm whether we should open TCP 443 and 9001 for the control plane, and whether you need any additional IP ranges for telemetry ingestion?

Also, we have an internal compliance review on Nov 5 — if possible, we'd like an inventory of the logs Redwood will retain and the retention durations.

Thanks,

Hi Aditi — thanks for the artifacts. I pulled in Ben (network lead) and Grace (deploy ops) so we can confirm specifics. Below is a short checklist mapped to what you sent; I've also attached our tenant-access-matrix.xlsx template to fill in the exact service-account names and network CIDRs.

Redwood pre-activation checklist (high priority):
1) Service accounts & roles
   - Provide exact SA email names for: control-plane-agent, telemetry-uploader, kms-sync. We require roles: roles/compute.networkUser (limited), roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter (for sync), custom read-only role for billing export access.
2) Egress / Control-plane reachability
   - Allow outbound TCP 443 to control.redwood.com (34.82.10.45) and TCP 9001 to control-stream.redwood.com (34.82.11.78) from the tenant NAT ranges.
   - If you have an allowlist requirement, provide the CIDR ranges in the tenant-access-matrix.xlsx.
3) KMS / secrets
   - We do not store customer keys; we need a service principal that can encrypt/decrypt a staging key to validate sync. Provide key resource name and policy snapshot.
4) Telemetry/log retention
   - By default Redwood retains agent logs for 30 days; audit logs forwarded to customer can be configured. We'll provide a short evidence pack for your compliance review.
5) Temporary troubleshooting access
   - Provide a single jump-host public IP (or transient Tailscale entry) for debug windows. Include an owner and time window.

Action items for Redwood:
- Ben: validate the port list and egress IPs for telemetry ingestion.
- Grace: prepare the compliance evidence pack (log samples + retention policy) by EOD Nov 4.

I attached: tenant-access-matrix.xlsx (template), edge-connection-diagram.pdf (example).

Would you be able to schedule a 30m synchronous window Tuesday (Nov 2) morning your time to walk the CIDRs? If not, we can do a recorded checklist review.

Best,
--
Mina Haddad

Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 1, 2027 at 17:04 +0000, mina_haddad@redwood.com wrote:
> Mina Haddad:
> > - Allow outbound TCP 443 to control.redwood.com (34.82.10.45) and TCP 9001 to control-stream.redwood.com (34.82.11.78) from the tenant NAT ranges.

Thanks for the clear mapping, Mina. A few network-specific clarifications from my side:

- Telemetry endpoints: we accept TLS on 443 for ingestion; the streaming control plane on 9001 uses mTLS (client cert) for session bootstrap — we'll need the client cert CN you plan to present (usually the control-plane-agent SA).
- NAT / Egress: If you have dynamic egress IPs (GCP Cloud NAT autoscaling), please provide a 72-hour window of expected ranges or a CIDR superset. If not available, we'll accept a signed attest and a <48h cutover with pre-notified IPs.
- MTU / path MTU: Make sure large payloads can pass — recommend MTU >= 1400 on the path to control-stream.redwood.com.
- Health checks: We will run a pre-activation HTTP/200 probe on /healthz from our monitoring region (us-west2). Please ensure that path is routable and not blocked by application firewalls.

Ben Carter
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
